title: Multi‐Sources and Modes‐Based Overtopping Risk Model for Gravity Dams Under Extreme Working Conditions
content:
Abstract

Addressing the limitations of traditional overtopping risk analysis methods, which either consider only a single failure mode or fail to accurately characterize the nonlinear characteristics of reservoir levels, this paper proposes a novel overtopping risk model for dams. According to the main modes of dam overtopping, a Bayesian network (BN) overtopping risk model including failure modes of flood, landslide surge, and gate failure for the gravity dams is put forward. By using the response surface method and the D-optimal design method, a segmented high-order response surface equation (H-RSE) for reservoir level is developed, solving the difficult problem of the water level being difficult to describe the impact of the flood peak discharge, initial water level, discharge coefficients, etc., then the flood overtopping risk analysis model is proposed. Additionally, the overtopping risk analysis model induced by gate failure and the risk model induced by landslide surge are established, forming the overtopping risk BN model for dams. Engineering application shows the average relative error of H-RSE is 2.35%, the flood overtopping is the most hazardous failure mode, and the main risk control factor is the extreme flood. The proposed model provides an effective approach for the overtopping risk analysis of high dams.
